description: Hi! I’m a student passionate about space, tech and solving real-world problems. I enjoy coding, working with data and turning ideas into working apps. Join my team to build a real demo, learn a lot and have fun! Beginners welcome, everyone gets a role. Looking for: developers (web/app), data/AI enthusiasts, designers (UI/video) and presenters. Most of all, motivated people committed for the full hackathon. Let’s build something amazing! 🚀
summary: AstroKids Academy is a web game that turns NASA space science into a training adventure for children aged 6-10. Kids design their own astronaut, explore an interactive 3D solar system with facts based on NASA data, see a space picture from NASA on their home page, play five astronaut-training mini-games (zero gravity, navigation, equipment, Moon landing, emergency rescue), build and launch a rocket, and chat with AstroBot, a safe AI space helper. They earn XP, level up, unlock badges and finish with a printable Junior Astronaut certificate. Parents create and manage the account, see learning progress and control AI use. The project addresses "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" by making NASA data and space exploration easy and fun to understand for young learners, building early interest in science and space careers. It runs on laptops, tablets and phones.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Children enter a virtual space academy. They create an astronaut avatar, explore a 3D solar system (Sun and eight planets with facts, sizes, distances and temperatures based on NASA data), and complete five playable missions that teach how astronauts move in zero gravity, navigate, use equipment, land on the Moon and handle emergencies. In the Rocket Lab they drag and drop rocket parts, test, and launch. AstroBot answers space questions in simple English. XP, levels, badges and a PDF certificate reward progress.

NASA DATA USED

- NASA Image and Video Library (images.nasa.gov): space pictures shown on the home page, credited to NASA.

- NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day API (api.nasa.gov): used when it returns a real photo.

- NASA Solar System Exploration and NASA Planetary Fact Sheet: the basis for planet facts in the app.

HOW IT WORKS

React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js (React Three Fiber) and Framer Motion for the interface and 3D scene. FastAPI, SQLAlchemy and Pydantic for the backend, with SQLite (MySQL supported). Rewards are calculated on the server, so scores cannot be faked, and every reward can be earned only once. Certificates are generated with ReportLab. The code has automated tests (28 backend, 4 frontend).

SAFETY AND PRIVACY

Accounts are managed by a parent. Only an email, a nickname and an age group are stored. AstroBot blocks personal information and unsafe topics, has a daily question limit, and parents can switch it off or delete its history. Without an API key it shows curated answers clearly labelled "demo mode".

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Children learn space facts and basic ideas such as gravity, thrust and safety procedures through play, while parents can follow progress. It is designed to build curiosity about NASA and STEM careers.

CREATIVITY

Everything is drawn in code (astronaut, rocket, robot, planets, certificate) and the sounds are synthesised in the browser, so it works without downloaded art or audio. A 2D fallback keeps it usable on devices without 3D graphics.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

Child privacy, parent control, accessibility (keyboard, touch, reduced motion), performance on ordinary laptops and phones, and graceful behaviour when NASA services are slow.
